mainTopic: הבלעת תחומין, rescuers returning home, fighting on שבת, and a traveler's שבת base without intention
overview: The amud opens with אביי challenging רבה from רבי אליעזר, who lets a person back into his תחום after 2 אמות but not 3. This suggests that overlapping boundaries (הבלעת תחומין) matter, and אביי adds that for a דבר מצוה even the רבנן agree. Next the גמרא asks how far people who go out to save lives may return. רב יהודה says the משנה means they may come home carrying their weapons, and a ברייתא tells of a deadly incident that led to this rule. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers differently: it depends on whether the Jews won or lost the battle. The גמרא then teaches when we may fight besieging gentiles on שבת: not over money alone, yes over lives, and in a border town such as נהרדעא even over hay and straw. The story of דוד and קעילה is brought, and the גמרא explains that דוד asked ה׳ only whether he would win. A new משנה follows: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue whether a traveler who unknowingly rested near a town may enter it, and the proof from רבי טרפון is pushed aside. A last משנה discusses a person who slept as שבת began, giving several views on his walking space and starting the case of two people whose areas overlap, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting רבי אליעזר on walking two or three cubits out
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה: according to רבי אליעזר, someone who stepped 2 אמות beyond his תחום may come back in, but 3 אמות may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in a משנה: רבי אליעזר says, if he went two cubits out, he may come back in; if three, he may not come back in?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source from a משנה to attack רבה's view. This step only sets up the source; the actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a person who went just past his שבת boundary (תחום). רבי אליעזר draws the line between 2 אמות out, where he may return, and 3 אמות out, where he may not. Why the line falls exactly there is what the next step uses to build the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה? This opens a challenge from a משנה.
The Shabbos boundary of 2000 אמות that a person may not walk past.
He may come back in (to his original boundary).
A cubit, roughly one and a half to two feet.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If he went two cubits out, he may come back in,
If he went three, he may not come back in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's challenge against רבה from the previous part of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that הבלעת תחומין is not significant.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being allowed back in after 2 אמות but not after 3 suggests that overlap is what counts. The next step spells this out.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's rule depends on overlapping boundaries
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a person standing in the middle of his 4 אמות reaches 2 אמות back. So at 2 אמות out, his area overlaps the original תחום. This proves that overlap matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that רבי אליעזר follows his own reasoning, since he says a person stands in the middle of his four cubits? The four cubits the רבנן gave him are treated as if they are swallowed into the original boundary, and that is why he said 'he may come back in.' So we see that overlapping boundaries are something real.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אליעזר's rule proves that הבלעת תחומין counts, and so challenges רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every person gets 4 אמות wherever he is. רבי אליעזר holds that he stands in their center, so he can reach 2 אמות in each direction. At 2 אמות out, those 2 אמות reach back into the original תחום. The two areas overlap, so he may re-enter. At 3 אמות out, they no longer touch. Overlap is the reason for the rule, which goes against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? This introduces a suggested reading of the source.
In the middle of them, meaning the person stands in the center of his 4 אמות.

steps.confusionAlert: The 4 אמות here are not the 2000-אמה תחום. They are the small personal area every person gets wherever he stands. Because he stands in the middle, he can reach exactly 2 אמות back, and that explains the 2-versus-3 line.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key question of the passage: does an overlapping boundary let a person pass back into his original area?

phrases.english: Is it not that Rabbi Eliezer follows his own reasoning,
for he said: and he is in the middle of them (his four cubits),
and the four cubits that the Rabbis gave him
are regarded as if they are swallowed into (overlap) the original boundary,
and so he says 'he may come back in.'
Apparently, overlapping of boundaries is something significant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה just quoted and turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's position that הבלעת תחומין does not matter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's 2-versus-3 line only makes sense if the overlap of the personal 4 אמות with the original תחום lets him back in.

steps.title: Why challenge רבה from רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה asks אביי why he would challenge רבה from רבי אליעזר's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said to אביי: Are you challenging the Master from רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה questions whether the challenge is fair, since it rests on the opinion of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's view is one side of a dispute with the רבנן. רבה could simply say he follows the רבנן, so a proof from רבי אליעזר alone seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the one asking the question here.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Hana said to Abaye:
And from Rabbi Eliezer you challenge the Master?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the strength of אביי's challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a view held only by רבי אליעזר can be used to challenge רבה.

steps.title: The Rabbis agree with רבי אליעזר for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: אביי says yes. He heard from רבה himself that the רבנן only disagree with רבי אליעזר in a voluntary case, and agree with him in a case of מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, because I heard from the Master himself: the רבנן only disagree with רבי אליעזר about a voluntary matter, but about a מצוה matter they agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his challenge. When someone went out for a מצוה, even the רבנן accept רבי אליעזר's overlap rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן is narrower than it looked. For a דבר מצוה, everyone agrees that overlap lets a person back in. Since רבה himself taught this, the challenge against רבה still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree up to this point. This limits the scope of a dispute.
A matter done for a מצוה.

steps.whatToRemember: For a דבר מצוה, everyone (רבי אליעזר and the רבנן) agrees that overlapping boundaries let a person return. So the challenge to רבה is built on a view all sides accept.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
for I heard it from the Master himself:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Eliezer only
regarding a voluntary matter,
but regarding a מצוה matter they agree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, דִּשְׁמִיעַ לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה בר בר חנה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן agree with רבי אליעזר in a case of מצוה, so the challenge is valid even according to the רבנן.

steps.title: Mishna: those who go out to save lives return home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: everyone who goes out to save lives may return to their places.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all who go out to save lives return to their places.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows rescuers who left their תחום on שבת to go back home. The next step asks how far 'return to their places' reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who go out to rescue (lives).

phrases.english: And all who go out to save lives
return to their places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rescuers who left their תחום may return to their original places.

steps.title: Even from very far? The first clause said only 2000 cubits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether rescuers may return from any distance at all, since the משנה's earlier clause allowed only 2000 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even from very far? But you said in the first clause: '2000 cubits,' and no more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction inside the משנה about how far rescuers may travel back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Return to their places' sounds unlimited. But the earlier clause gave a person who went out with permission only 2000 אמות from where he ends up. The two parts of the משנה seem to clash.

phrases.english: Even from a great distance?
But didn't you say in the first clause:
'two thousand cubits,' and no more!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause limits a person to 2000 אמות, so an unlimited return contradicts it.

steps.title: רב explains the real point: they return with their weapons
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב answers Step 6. The משנה's new point is not about unlimited distance. It is that the rescuers may go back home carrying their weapons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the משנה means that they may return to their places with their weapons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6. The משנה is teaching that rescuers may carry their weapons back home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 assumed the משנה meant rescuers may return from any distance, which seemed to clash with the 2000 אמות limit. רב shifts the focus. The new point is what they may bring back (their weapons), not how far they may go. That removes the clash.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
that they return with weapons to their places.
phrases.notes: The new point is that they may return carrying their weapons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 6 by reading the משנה differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's new point (weapons, not distance)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lets rescuers return home from any distance, against the 2000 אמות limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is teaching that rescuers may return carrying their weapons.

steps.title: Why was that even a question? Saving lives may be different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the question of Step 6 itself. Maybe rescuers really may return from any distance, because saving lives is a special case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what was the difficulty? Perhaps the case of going out to save lives is different!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and says the question from Step 6 was not strong to begin with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 compared rescuers to the earlier clause of the משנה, which gives only 2000 אמות. The גמרא now says rescuers are a special category, so there is no contradiction even if they return from far away. This clears the way for a stronger difficulty in the next step.

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps going out to save lives is different!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question of Step 6 and rejects it as weak.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קשיא of Step 6 (and so the need for רב's answer).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question ignored that saving lives may be a special case with no distance limit.

steps.title: The real difficulty begins: the witnesses in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces the real difficulty by quoting a משנה. At first, the witnesses of the new moon could not move from their courtyard all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty. As we learned: at first, they would not move from there the entire day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a stronger question by starting to quote a משנה from ראש השנה. The question itself comes in Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted משנה is about witnesses who traveled on שבת to testify about the new moon. Originally they were stuck in the courtyard where they arrived and could not walk around at all. This sets up the rule that someone who leaves his תחום for a מצוה gets only limited movement where he arrives.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty:
as we learned: At first
phrases.notes: A משנה in ראש השנה about the new-moon witnesses.

phrases.english: they would not move from there
the entire day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the weak question, the גמרא opens a stronger one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The line of our משנה: everyone who goes out to save lives may return to their places.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The quoted משנה will show that rescuers get only 2000 אמות.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's enactment: 2000 אמות for witnesses, midwives, and rescuers
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues. רבן גמליאל הזקן enacted that the witnesses get 2000 אמות in every direction. The same applies to a midwife and to rescuers, who are treated like the people of the town they reach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל הזקן enacted that they have 2000 אמות in every direction. And not only these did they say, but even a midwife who comes to deliver a baby, and one who comes to rescue from troops, from a river, from a collapsed building, or from a fire: they are like the people of the town, and they have 2000 אמות in every direction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה. It gives rescuers only 2000 אמות from the place they reach, and this sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new rule makes the newcomers like residents of the town they arrived at. They get a normal 2000-אמה תחום measured from there. It says nothing about returning to their own home if that is farther away.

keyTerms.meaning: like the residents of the town

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכׇל רוּחַ.
phrases.english: that they have two thousand cubits in every direction.
And not only these did they say,
but even a midwife who comes to deliver a baby,
and one who comes to rescue from invading troops

phrases.aramaic: וּמִן הַנָּהָר וּמִן הַמַּפּוֹלֶת וּמִן הַדְּלֵיקָה
phrases.english: or from a river, or from a collapsed building, or from a fire
they are like the residents of the town,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ לָהֶן אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכׇל רוּחַ.
phrases.english: and they have two thousand cubits in every direction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quote of the משנה begun in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses, a midwife, and rescuers are like the residents of the town they reach and have 2000 אמות in every direction.

steps.title: Only 2000 אמות? But our משנה lets rescuers return home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the contradiction. The משנה in ראש השנה gives rescuers only 2000 אמות. Our משנה says all rescuers may return to their places, even from far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And no more than that? But you said: all who go out to save lives may return to their places, even from a great distance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks its real question. The two משניות seem to disagree about how far rescuers may walk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ראש השנה משנה limits rescuers to 2000 אמות from where they arrive. Our משנה lets them go all the way home, even if that is farther. This is a stronger question than Step 6, because both sources are talking about rescuers. The answer "saving lives is different" does not work here.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the question in Step 6. That question compared rescuers to other people. This one compares rescuers to rescuers, in two different משניות.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer to this contradiction will decide how far a rescuer may walk home on שבת after saving lives.

phrases.english: And no more than that?
But didn't you say:
all who go out to save lives return to their places
even from a great distance!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה quoted in Steps 9 and 10 to challenge our משנה (Step 5).
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה: everyone who goes out to save lives may return to their places.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ראש השנה משנה limits rescuers to 2000 אמות from where they arrive. Our משנה lets them return home from any distance. Both are about rescuers, so they seem to contradict.

steps.title: Our משנה is about returning with weapons, not about unlimited distance
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב resolves the contradiction from Step 11. Our משנה's new point is that rescuers may go back carrying their weapons. It does not give them unlimited distance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: our משנה means that they go back to their places carrying their weapons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between our משנה and the משנה in ראש השנה. It repeats the line from Step 7, but now it is used as the answer to Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 read our משנה as giving rescuers unlimited distance, which clashed with the 2000 אמות in ראש השנה. רב יהודה rejects that reading. The rescuers still get only 2000 אמות. The new point is that they may carry their weapons as they walk back. Now the two משניות agree.

keyTerms.meaning: to their places (where they came from)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a repeat of Step 7. There, this line answered a question about our משנה alone. Here, the same line resolves a contradiction between two different משניות.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
that they return with weapons to their places,
phrases.notes: The new point is carrying the weapons. The distance is still limited to 2000 אמות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שֶׁחוֹזְרִין בִּכְלֵי זַיִין לִמְקוֹמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the contradiction stated in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of our משנה's new point (weapons, not distance)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה lets rescuers return home from any distance, which contradicts the 2000 אמות limit in ראש השנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both משניות allow only 2000 אמות. Our משנה only adds that the rescuers may carry their weapons back.

steps.title: The story behind allowing rescuers to carry weapons home
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב יהודה. Rescuers used to leave their weapons in the house nearest the wall. Once, enemies chased them in and there was deadly chaos, so the חכמים enacted that they return home carrying their weapons.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: At first, the rescuers would leave their weapons in the house next to the city wall. Once, the enemies recognized them and chased after them. The rescuers ran in to grab their weapons, and the enemies came in after them. They pushed against each other and killed each other, more than the enemies killed. At that time, the חכמים enacted that they should return to their places with their weapons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the rule about carrying weapons home really exists, and to explain where it came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying weapons on שבת is normally a problem, so at first the rescuers put them down as soon as they reached the wall. That made the rescuers defenseless, and it led to a deadly crush in one small house. So the חכמים made a תקנה allowing them to keep their weapons with them all the way back. This supports רב יהודה's claim that our משנה's חידוש is about the weapons.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the חכמים changing a שבת practice because real lives were lost. Safety can override a stricter practice.

phrases.english: As it was taught (in a baraita):
At first they would put down their weapons
in the house next to the wall.
Once, enemies noticed them
and chased after them,
and they went in to take their weapons,
and the enemies came in after them.
They pushed against one another,
and they killed one another
more than the enemies killed.
At that time they enacted
that they should return to their places with their weapons.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין כְּלֵי זֵיינָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's answer by showing the source of the weapons rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's claim that the חידוש of our משנה is returning with weapons
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording a תקנה made after a deadly incident

steps.title: A second answer: it depends on who won the battle
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different answer. The משנה in ראש השנה (only 2000 אמות) is about when the Jews won. Our משנה (go all the way home) is about when the Jews lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is not difficult. Here, it is when the Jews defeated the nations of the world. There, it is when the nations of the world defeated 'themselves' (meaning the Jews).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different way to resolve the contradiction from Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק keeps the simple reading: our משנה really does allow returning from far away. He explains that the two משניות discuss different situations. When the Jews win, there is no danger, so they get only 2000 אמות. When the Jews lose, staying where they are is dangerous, so they may go all the way home.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (there is no contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם defeated themselves' does not mean the gentiles beat themselves. 'Themselves' (אֶת עַצְמָן) is a polite way of saying 'the Jews', to avoid writing that the Jews lost.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. רב יהודה says our משנה is about carrying weapons, within 2000 אמות. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it depends on who won: Jews won means 2000 אמות, Jews lost means they may go all the way home.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is not difficult.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — שֶׁנִּצְּחוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: Here — when Israel defeated the nations of the world,
phrases.notes: The משנה in ראש השנה: only 2000 אמות.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — שֶׁנִּצְּחוּ אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֶת עַצְמָן.
phrases.english: here — when the nations of the world defeated 'themselves' (i.e., Israel).
phrases.notes: Our משנה: they may return home even from far away.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different resolution of Step 11, parallel to רב יהודה's answer in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): victory versus defeat
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות give opposite rules for the same rescuers.
steps.terutzMaskana: After a Jewish victory, rescuers get only 2000 אמות. After a Jewish defeat, they may go all the way home for safety.

steps.title: Gentiles besieging Jewish towns: no going out to fight on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Moving to a related topic, רב יהודה in the name of רב rules that when gentiles besiege Jewish towns, we do not go out against them with weapons and do not break שבת because of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When gentiles besiege Jewish towns, we do not go out against them with weapons, and we do not break שבת because of them.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא was discussing war on שבת, it now brings a new statement about a siege. This opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule here is that a siege by itself does not permit going out to fight or breaking שבת. This seems to clash with the earlier idea that we may go out to save people. That signals that the גמרא will soon need to explain which kind of siege this rule is talking about.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement starts the discussion of when a threat from gentiles allows breaking שבת. It is a basic source for the הלכות of war and self-defense on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Gentiles who besieged Jewish towns —
we do not go out against them with their weapons,
and we do not desecrate שבת because of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב נׇכְרִים שֶׁצָּרוּ עַל עַיְירוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related topic (war on שבת), prompted by the discussion of rescuers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When gentiles besiege Jewish towns, we do not go out with weapons against them and do not break שבת because of them (details to follow).

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב יהודה's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a ברייתא that teaches the same rule as רב יהודה: gentiles who besiege a town are not fought with weapons on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: 'Gentiles who besieged, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing רב יהודה said in Step 15. This sets up the details the ברייתא adds next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's ruling now has backing from a תנאי source. The word וכו׳ is shorthand for the full rule: we do not go out with weapons and do not break שבת. The ברייתא will now add an important limit to that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא
Etcetera; the rest of the quote is understood

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
Gentiles who besieged, etc.
phrases.notes: Refers back to the full rule of רב יהודה: no weapons, no breaking שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the מימרא of רב יהודה in Step 15
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's rule that we do not fight besieging gentiles on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording

steps.title: The rule applies only when they come for money
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the rule to attacks about money. If the attackers threaten lives, we go out with weapons and break שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When they came about money matters. But if they came about lives, we go out against them with weapons and break שבת for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains when the 'don't fight on שבת' rule applies. It applies only when the gentiles are after money, not lives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 15 is narrowed. Robbery alone does not justify breaking שבת. Danger to life (פיקוח נפש) does, so then we fight with weapons even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (introduces a limit)
Money matters, such as robbery or plunder
Matters of life, a threat to kill

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read Step 15 as 'never fight on שבת.' That rule covers only money-motivated attacks. When lives are threatened, fighting on שבת is permitted.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
When they came over money matters;
but if they came over matters of life —
they go out against them with their weapons,
and they desecrate Shabbat on their account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and limits its rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The no-fighting rule applies only to money-motivated sieges. When lives are threatened, we fight and break שבת.

steps.title: A border town fights back even over hay and straw
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that in a town near the border, we fight on שבת even if the gentiles only came to take hay and straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in a town near the border, even if they came not about lives but only about hay and straw, we go out against them with weapons and break שבת for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second exception. A town on the border must defend itself on שבת even against a small raid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a money raid does not permit breaking שבת. A border town is different: if enemies gain a foothold there, the whole land becomes open to attack. So even a raid for hay and straw counts as a real danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Hay and straw; something of very little value

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the danger is judged by location, not only by what the attackers are after.

phrases.english: And in a town that is near the border,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לֹא בָּאוּ עַל עִסְקֵי נְפָשׁוֹת
phrases.english: even if they did not come over matters of life
but only over matters of hay and straw —
they go out against them with their weapons,
and they desecrate Shabbat on their account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second exception within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A border town may fight on שבת even against a raid for hay and straw.

steps.title: בבל, specifically נהרדעא, counts as a border town
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that בבל has the status of a border town. The גמרא explains that this refers to the city of נהרדעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: בבל is like a town near the border. And this is explained to mean נהרדעא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן applies the border-town rule to בבל. The גמרא then narrows it: he meant נהרדעא, which sat near the border.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes the rule from Step 18 and applies it to a real place. The word ותרגומא clarifies that not all of בבל is included, only נהרדעא. So in נהרדעא, people may fight on שבת even against a money raid.

keyTerms.meaning: Is similar to, has the same status as
And its explanation is (introduces a clarification)
נהרדעא, a city in בבל near the border

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels: a money raid means no fighting on שבת. A threat to life means fight. A border town (such as נהרדעא) means fight even over hay and straw.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Manyumi said that Rav Naḥman said:
And Babylonia is like a town near the border.
And its explanation: Neharde'a.
phrases.notes: Narrows רב נחמן's statement to the border city of נהרדעא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the border-town exception of Step 18 to a real place
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נהרדעא in בבל has the status of a border town for fighting on שבת.

steps.title: רבי דוסתאי asks about the פסוק of דוד and קעילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי of בירי opens a דרשה, asking what the פסוק about the Philistines attacking קעילה and robbing the threshing floors means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסתאי of בירי expounded: What is the meaning of the verse, 'And they told דוד, saying: Behold, the Philistines are fighting against קעילה, and they are robbing the threshing floors'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי begins a דרשה on a פסוק about a Philistine raid. This is a setup line; the ברייתא in Step 21 gives the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק fits our topic: gentiles raiding a border town for grain, a money matter. Asking 'what does this verse mean' prepares a lesson about why דוד needed to ask whether to fight such a raid.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded, taught a lesson from a פסוק
What is the meaning of what is written?
Threshing floors, where grain is processed

phrases.english: Rabbi Dostai of Biri expounded:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"And they told David, saying:
Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Ke'ila,
and they are robbing the threshing floors" (I Samuel 23:1).

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי דְּמִן בֵּירֵי מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a דרשה on a פסוק about a border-town raid, related to Step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the פסוק about the Philistine raid on קעילה teaches

steps.title: קעילה was a border town attacked only for hay and straw
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers רבי דוסתאי's question. קעילה was a town near the border, and the Philistines came only for hay and straw, as the פסוק says they were robbing the threshing floors.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: קעילה was a town near the border, and the Philistines came only for hay and straw, as it is written: 'And they are robbing the threshing floors.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the פסוק about קעילה. It tells us two facts: the town was on the border, and the attackers only wanted hay and straw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two facts match the case in Step 18 exactly: a border town, and an attack over small property. The proof is that 'robbing the threshing floors' shows they wanted crops and straw, not lives.

keyTerms.meaning: Ke'ila, a town in the land of יהודה
Hay and straw, things of little value
Threshing floors, where grain is processed

phrases.english: It was taught: Ke'ila was a town
that was near the border,
and they came only
over matters of hay and straw,
as it is written: 'And they are robbing the threshing floors.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: קְעִילָה עִיר הַסְּמוּכָה לַסְּפָר הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question opened by רבי דוסתאי in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the פסוק about the Philistines robbing the threshing floors of קעילה teach?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קעילה was a border town, and the attack was only over hay and straw.

steps.title: ה׳ tells דוד to go fight and save קעילה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with the next פסוק. דוד asked ה׳ whether to fight, and ה׳ told him to go and save קעילה. This supports fighting for a border town even over hay and straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'דוד asked ה׳: Shall I go and strike these Philistines? And ה׳ said to דוד: Go, strike the Philistines, and save קעילה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quotes the next פסוק. In it, ה׳ tells דוד to go fight for קעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Put together with Step 21, the picture is: a border town, an attack only over property, and still a command to go fight. This fits the rule of Step 18, that a border town fights back on שבת even over hay and straw.

keyTerms.meaning: דוד asked of ה׳ (through the אורים ותומים)

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And David asked of ה׳, saying:
Shall I go and strike these Philistines?
And ה׳ said to David:
Go, and strike the Philistines,
and save Ke'ila.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by adding the command to fight.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a border town fights back even over hay and straw.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ה׳'s command to דוד: 'Go, strike the Philistines, and save קעילה.'

steps.title: What was דוד asking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what דוד's question was. It cannot have been whether fighting was permitted, because the בית דין of שמואל was there to rule on halachic questions.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was he unsure about? If you say he asked whether it was permitted or forbidden, the בית דין of שמואל הרמתי was still active!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly דוד asked ה׳. It rules out the idea that he was asking a halachic question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Halachic questions go to a בית דין, not to prophecy or the אורים ותומים. Since שמואל's court was active at that time, דוד would have asked them. So his question to ה׳ must have been about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: The court of שמואל from רמה

steps.confusionAlert: This question does not cancel the lesson about border towns. It only clarifies that דוד was not asking ה׳ whether fighting was allowed. That halacha could be answered by the בית דין.

phrases.english: What was he unsure about?
If you say: whether it is permitted or forbidden —
but the court of
Shmuel of Ramah was in existence!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָמִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ? אִילֵּימָא אִי שְׁרֵי אִי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the פסוק just quoted, asking what דוד's question was.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was the content of דוד's question to ה׳?

steps.title: דוד asked whether he would succeed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that דוד was asking whether he would win the battle, not whether fighting was allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he asked whether he would succeed or not succeed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer: דוד wanted to know if he would win.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This kind of question about the future belongs to prophecy, not to a בית דין. So asking ה׳ makes sense, and there is no contradiction with the existence of שמואל's court.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: אִי מַצְלַח אִי לָא מַצְלַח.
phrases.english: Rather: whether he will succeed or will not succeed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אִי מַצְלַח אִי לָא מַצְלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דוד asked whether he would succeed in battle.

steps.title: The wording of ה׳'s answer confirms it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the פסוק's wording supports this reading. ה׳'s answer, 'strike the Philistines and save קעילה', is a promise of victory.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also precise, as it is written: 'Go, strike the Philistines, and save קעילה.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds support in the פסוק's own words for the answer of Step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ did not just say 'it is permitted.' He promised a result: you will strike them and save the town. An answer about the outcome shows that the question was about the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: This is also precise (the wording supports it)

steps.whatToRemember: קעילה shows that a border town is defended even over hay and straw. דוד asked ה׳ only whether he would win, because halachic questions went to שמואל's בית דין.

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it is written:
'Go, and strike the Philistines,
and save Ke'ila,'
learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 24 from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד asked whether he would succeed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ה׳'s answer promising victory: 'strike the Philistines and save קעילה'.

steps.title: A traveler who rested near a town without intending to may not enter
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. Someone sat on the road before שבת. After שבת began he stood up and saw he was close to a town, within its 2000 אמות. Since he did not intend to make the town his שבת base, רבי מאיר says he may not enter it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sat on the road, then stood up and saw that he was near a town: since that was not his intention, he may not enter. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new משנה with a new topic: how a traveler's שבת boundary is set when he didn't plan it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether being near the town automatically lets him use it as his base. רבי מאיר says no: without intention, he does not acquire the town. His 2000 אמות are measured from where he sat, so he cannot walk through the whole town.

keyTerms.meaning: Near the town (within its שבת limit)

steps.confusionAlert: 'May not enter' does not mean he can't move at all. He still has 2000 אמות from where he sat. He just doesn't get the whole town as his own.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who sat on the road,
and stood up and saw
that he was near the town,
since this was not his intention —
he may not enter.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic after the קעילה discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a person who unknowingly rested within a town's שבת limit, without intending to acquire it, may not enter the town on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says he may enter the town
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר and allows the person to enter the town.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He may enter.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second opinion. רבי יהודה rules that the person may go into the town even though he never planned to make it his שבת base.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר required a real intention to make the town his base. רבי יהודה holds that being within 2000 אמות of the town is enough, even without that intention. The whole argument is about whether intention is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who argues with רבי מאיר here

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He may enter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opinion that disagrees with רבי מאיר's ruling in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intention to make the town your base is not required. Being within its 2000 אמות is enough to enter.

steps.title: רבי יהודה cites רבי טרפון's story
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה supports his view with an event in which רבי טרפון entered a town without having intended it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: It once happened that רבי טרפון entered a town without having intended it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה backs up his ruling with a real event. רבי טרפון entered a town on שבת even though he had not planned to make it his base.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מעשה, a real event involving a great sage, counts as strong evidence for how the halacha works in practice. If רבי טרפון entered without intention, it seems that intention is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It once happened (a story brought as proof)
A great תנא, the sage in the story

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
It once happened that Rabbi Tarfon entered
without intending it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יהודה's ruling in step 27 with a real event.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's ruling that one may enter without intention
steps.raayaSupportSource: The event of רבי טרפון entering a town

steps.title: The full story of רבי טרפון from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that tells the רבי טרפון story in full detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה said: It happened that רבי טרפון was traveling on the road, night fell, and he slept outside the town. In the morning, cowherds found him and said: רבי, the town is right in front of you, come in! He went in, sat in the בית המדרש, and taught the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section on this משנה opens by quoting a ברייתא that tells the full story. It explains exactly how רבי טרפון ended up entering the town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The details make the proof sound stronger. רבי טרפון was simply caught by nightfall, and only in the morning did he learn the town was close. He then entered and stayed there all day, which suggests he had no earlier plan to make it his base.

keyTerms.meaning: And night fell on him (שבת began)

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
It happened with Rabbi Tarfon
that he was walking on the road and night fell on him,
and he spent the night outside the town.
In the morning cowherds found him,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: רַבִּי, הֲרֵי הָעִיר לְפָנֶיךָ, הִכָּנֵס!
phrases.english: they said to him: Master, the town is in front of you, enter!
He entered and sat in the study hall,
and taught the entire day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the short story from step 28 with the full ברייתא version.
steps.raayaObject: That entering a town without earlier intention is allowed
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא telling the story of רבי טרפון

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof from רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים give two other explanations of the story, so it proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that your proof? Maybe he did have it in mind, or maybe the בית המדרש was already within his 2000 אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's proof. They give two other ways to explain why רבי טרפון was allowed to enter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, maybe רבי טרפון did plan before שבת to make the town his base, even though he did not say so. Second, maybe the בית המדרש was close enough to fall inside the 2000 אמות from where he slept, and then everyone agrees he could go there. Either way, the story does not show that intention is unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? (a rejection formula)
Perhaps he had it in mind

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying רבי טרפון did something wrong. They are saying his entering was allowed for a different reason, so it cannot prove רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: A story can only prove a rule if there is no other way to explain it. Here the story has two other explanations, so the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה stays open.

phrases.english: (They said to him:) Is that a proof?
Perhaps it was in his mind,
or the study hall was included
within his Shabbat boundary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 28 and 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the story. It does not disprove רבי יהודה's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story can be explained without assuming he lacked intention: either he did intend it, or the בית המדרש was inside his תחום anyway.

steps.title: New משנה: a person who slept on the road when שבת began
steps.stepSummary: A person who slept through the start of שבת still gets 2000 אמות in every direction, according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who fell asleep on the road and did not know that night had come gets 2000 אמות in every direction. These are the words of רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case. A person was asleep when שבת started, so he had no awareness or intention at all, and the משנה asks whether he still gets a שבת area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that simply being in a place when שבת begins gives you a base there, even without knowing it. So the sleeper gets 2000 אמות around him in every direction. This connects to the earlier argument about whether intention is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 2000 אמות, the standard שבת walking range
The תנא who gives this ruling

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the view that a person gains a שבת base automatically, just by being in a place, with no thought or intention needed.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who slept on the road
and did not know that night had fallen,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכׇל רוּחַ,
phrases.english: has two thousand cubits in every direction,
these are the words of Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיָּשַׁן בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְלָא יָדַע שֶׁחָשֵׁיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new case about a person who had no awareness at all when שבת began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person asleep when שבת begins still gets a base where he is, with 2000 אמות in every direction (רבי יוחנן בן נורי).

steps.title: The חכמים limit the sleeper to four cubits
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי יוחנן בן נורי and say the sleeper gets only ארבע אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the חכמים say: he has only four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposing view to רבי יוחנן בן נורי. The חכמים say the person who slept gets only ארבע אמות of walking space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי held that a sleeper automatically gets a תחום of 2000 אמות. The חכמים hold that you only gain a תחום if you are awake and aware when שבת begins. A sleeper did not knowingly set up a place for himself, so he is left with the bare minimum of ארבע אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, the small space anyone may move in on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The ארבע אמות is not in addition to 2000 אמות. According to the חכמים, the sleeper has only ארבע אמות in total.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main disagreement: does a person gain a תחום automatically, or only when he is aware of it?

phrases.english: But the Sages say:
he has only four cubits.
phrases.notes: Because he did not knowingly gain a resting place when שבת began.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the opposing opinion to רבי יוחנן בן נורי in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sleeper does not gain a תחום. He may move only ארבע אמות.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר places the person in the middle
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר agrees there are only ארבע אמות, but says the person stands in their center.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: and he is in the middle of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר explains how the ארבע אמות are measured. The person stands in the center, with two אמות on each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר does not argue about the total amount. He agrees it is ארבע אמות. He only tells us where those ארבע אמות sit, so the person may move just two אמות in any direction.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives his own view on how the space is measured

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
and he is in the middle of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains how the חכמים's ארבע אמות are laid out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ארבע אמות are measured with the person in the middle, so he gets two אמות in each direction.

steps.title: רבי יהודה lets him choose a direction
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the person may walk his ארבע אמות in whichever direction he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: he may walk in whatever direction he wishes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a third way to use the ארבע אמות. The person may take all four in one direction of his choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר limited him to two אמות on each side. רבי יהודה lets him go a full ארבע אמות, but only in one direction that he picks. So the choice of direction is up to the person.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same רבי יהודה ruling as in step 27. There he spoke about entering a town. Here he is speaking about the sleeper's ארבע אמות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
he may walk in whatever direction he wishes.
phrases.notes: A full four cubits in the direction he chooses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This disagrees with רבי אליעזר about how the ארבע אמות are measured.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person may walk ארבע אמות in any one direction he chooses.

steps.title: Once he chooses, he cannot switch
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה agrees that once the person has picked a direction, he is locked into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה agrees that if he chose for himself, he cannot go back on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה puts a limit on רבי יהודה's freedom of choice. After picking a direction, the person may not switch to another one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this line, you might think he could walk four אמות one way, come back, and then walk four אמות another way. The word ומודה tells us רבי יהודה himself agrees to this limit. The choice is open only until he makes it.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees; introduces a point of agreement or a limit
To go back on it; to retract

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on the sleeper's space. The חכמים say he gets ארבע אמות. רבי אליעזר says he stands in the middle of them. רבי יהודה says he may pick any one direction, but once he picks, he cannot switch.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda agrees
that if he chose for himself
he cannot go back on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This limits רבי יהודה's ruling from step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once a direction has been chosen, it cannot be changed.

steps.title: Two people whose areas overlap
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a new case: two people whose ארבע אמות partly overlap may bring their food and eat in the shared middle area.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were two people, and part of one's four cubits was inside the other's four cubits, they may bring food and eat in the middle,
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves on to a new situation with two people standing close together. It says they may eat together in the shared space. This sentence continues on the next amud with a condition still to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person may use only his own ארבע אמות. The area where their spaces overlap belongs to both of them, so both may carry food into it and eat there together. The comma at the end shows that a limit on this permission is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: In the middle; here, the shared overlapping area

steps.confusionAlert: Here בָּאֶמְצַע means the shared overlap between two people's areas. It is not the same as רבי אליעזר's בְּאֶמְצָעָן, which meant the person stands at the center of his own ארבע אמות.

phrases.english: If there were two people,
and part of the cubits of this one
was inside the cubits of that one,
they may bring food and eat in the middle,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This builds on the ארבע אמות rule to set up a new case with two people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people whose ארבע אמות overlap may bring food and eat together in the shared area.
